knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Routine cleaning does not cover treatment of a damp room. The cleaner stops, and the scope is revised by the responsible manager after a competent assessment.
Mould follows moisture. The source must be found and corrected, and repainting over it does not solve the problem.
Recurring staining signals concealed damage. Demolition is not accepted on instruction alone and waits for a competent assessment.
Possible asbestos under contaminated water needs isolation and escalation. Disturbing it is not acceptable for an ordinary cleaner.
Health questions go to clinicians. A cleaner gives no clearance or medical statement.
PPE is matched to the evaluated exposure and the worker's training and fit are verified. A loose mask does not meet that standard.
Airborne particles can reach occupied areas, so containment and zoning are planned and approved before work begins.
Saturated porous materials cannot be reliably cleaned. Each material needs a classification and a competent decision, not a blanket method.
Dry brushing and domestic vacuums can throw spores into the air and are unsuitable for contaminated areas.
Demolition debris is not ordinary office waste. Disposal, transport and contractor authorisations are verified before handling.
Paint over a damp surface hides the problem and does not stop the mould. The source must be fixed and re-evaluated first.
A visual clean does not establish pathogen-free status. The closeout names what is not cleared and who must give independent clearance.

practicalCriteria: Produces a task-authorisation record for a simulated damp-room request that lists permitted inspection only, specialist referral, occupants and excluded destructive work.
Stops and escalates a simulated ceiling collapse with sewage-affected plasterboard and suspicious insulation, using a risk register, without disturbing the material.
Audits a simulated PPE selection and training record and escalates each deficiency found.
Compares proposed cleaning methods against an approved plan and identifies each unsuitable option with the reason.
Writes a factual closeout report that separates task completion, visual review and independent clearance, and names the areas not cleared.
passRule: Competent only if all five observable tasks are demonstrated correctly in supervised paper or training-only simulation with no critical safety failure. Critical failures include proceeding without site authority or a competent remediation supervisor, disturbing suspected asbestos or contaminated material, giving a clearance or medical statement, or accepting inadequate PPE. A written quiz pass is not practical competence. Not approved for use until specialist, legal and jurisdiction review is complete.
evidenceRequired: Task-authorisation record for each simulated case.
Stop-work decision tree and controlled referral note for a simulated concealed-damage case.
Risk register for the simulated isolation and escalation.
PPE audit record with deficiencies and escalations.
Closeout report from the simulated job file.
Assessor observation record signed by an organisation-authorised competent assessor.
stopWorkCriteria: Any work where the site authority or competent remediation supervisor is missing.
Any disturbance of material that may contain asbestos or lead, or of material in contaminated water, without competent assessment.
Any PPE or respirator use without the evaluated exposure, the programme, training and fit.
Any use of an unsuitable cleaning method or equipment in a contaminated area.
Any clearance, pathogen-free or medical statement.
Any waste removal or disposal without an authorised route.
